702885.t: From Old Median *ganǰam (“treasure”) spread by the Achaemenid administration.

702819.t: From βρέχω (brékhō, “to rain”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

702830.t: Traditionally considered a metathesis from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewb- (“hazy, deep”), with cognates including Old Church Slavonic дъно (dŭno), Old English dēop (English deep) and Albanian det (from Proto-Albanian *deubeta).

702812.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *mergʰ- (“to moisten, wet”) via a metathesized schwebeablaut form of *mregʰ- or zero-grade form *mr̥gʰ-; cognates include Latvian merguot (“to rain slowly”), merga (“soft rain”).

702808.t: From βραχύς (brăkhŭ́s, “short”) + -ίων (-ī́ōn, comparative suffix), literally “the shorter one”, because the upper arm is shorter than the forearm.

702823.t: From the root of βιβρώσκω (bibrṓskō, “to eat”) + -μα (-mă, object noun suffix).

702811.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʷrebʰ-. Cognates include Old Church Slavonic жрѣбѧ (žrěbę) ("foal") and Irish bromach ("colt").

702817.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mrətós, from Proto-Indo-European *mr̥tós (“dead, mortal”), ultimately from the root *mer- (“to die”).

702820.t: According to Beekes, the word might be of Pre-Greek origin if the connection with the Hesychian gloss βρυγχός (brunkhós) is reliable, which would show an instance of prenasalization.

702840.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷōmós, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷoh₂mós, from *gʷeh₂- (“to step”) (whence ἔβην (ébēn)). Compare βῆμα (bêmă, “step”).

702832.t: A loanword of unknown, possibly Pre-Greek, origin. Perhaps cognate with Hittite 𒆳𒊭𒀸 (kur-ša-aš); see there for more.

702814.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin, based on the alternating ρο/ορ vocalism.

702834.t: From a Semitic source cognate to Hebrew בּוּץ (būṣ, “byssus”) and Aramaic בּוּצָא (būṣā, “byssus”), from Proto-Semitic *būṣ- (“fibrous grass; rush”). Compare also Old Armenian բեհեզ (behez, “byssus”).

702839.t: Unknown; a candidate for Pre-Greek origin.
